title: The Need for Persistent Storage 💾
description: Understand why ephemeral Pods require durable storage solutions.

slides.title: Pods Are Ephemeral 🍂
slides.content:
# Data dies with the Pod

When a Pod is deleted (or its container restarts), any data written inside the container's filesystem is **gone forever**. That’s fine for stateless apps, but databases, caches, and file uploads need **persistence**.

Kubernetes provides **volumes** that outlive individual containers – and even Pods.

quizData.question: Why does a container’s local filesystem lose data on restart?

options.text: The writable layer is ephemeral and tied to the container lifecycle
Kubernetes deletes all files on restart

quizData.explanation: Container filesystems are temporary; only volumes persist beyond a container’s lifetime.

slides.title: Volume Fundamentals 📚
slides.content:
## What is a Volume?

A volume is a directory accessible to containers in a Pod. Unlike the container filesystem, volumes have a **lifetime independent of any single container**.

- Defined in the Pod spec (`spec.volumes`).
- Mounted into containers via `volumeMounts`.
- Can be backed by many types: emptyDir, hostPath, cloud disk, NFS, etc.

A volume exists as long as the Pod exists (unless it’s a PersistentVolume).

slides.title: Minimal Volume Example
slides.content: A Pod with an emptyDir volume shared between two containers:
slides.codeSnippet:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: shared-volume-pod
spec:
  volumes:
  - name: cache
    emptyDir: {}
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx
    volumeMounts:
    - name: cache
      mountPath: /cache
  - name: logger
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "while true; do echo $(date) >> /cache/log.txt; sleep 5; done"]
    volumeMounts:
    - name: cache
      mountPath: /cache

slides.title: Use Cases for Volumes 🗂️
slides.content:
## Common scenarios

- **Cache / temporary data**: emptyDir – deleted when Pod is removed.
- **Logs / metrics**: shared volume with a sidecar.
- **Config / secrets**: ConfigMap and Secret volumes (Chapter 5).
- **Persistent data**: cloud disk, NFS – outlives Pod and even node.
- **Container-to-container communication**: via shared files.

quizData.question: Which volume type’s lifetime is tied to the Pod?
quizData.explanation: emptyDir is created when the Pod is assigned to a node and deleted when the Pod is removed.
